Saying: The Lord works in mysterious ways
WhatItMeans: People usually take it to mean that God has a hidden plan behind confusing or painful events, and that what looks senseless now will make sense in time.
WhatTheBibleSays: Scripture does teach that God's ways are beyond ours: "For my thoughts are not your thoughts, neither are your ways my ways, saith the LORD" (Isaiah 55:8), and Romans 11:33 calls His judgments unsearchable and His ways past finding out, while Psalm 77:19 says His footsteps are not known. But the Bible never promises that every mystery will be explained to us in this life; it calls us to trust His character when we cannot trace His hand. I believe the thought behind the line is sound, but the words themselves are a hymn writer's, not Scripture's.
Origin: William Cowper's hymn "God Moves in a Mysterious Way", written in 1773 under its original title "Light Shining out of Darkness" and first published in 1774 in John Newton's Twenty-six Letters on Religious Subjects.
RelatedTopics: God's Providence; God's Sovereignty; Trust; Suffering; Hope
Sources: Cowper, 'God Moves in a Mysterious Way' (written 1773, published 1774); on-site KJV text of Psalm 77:19, Isaiah 55:8-9 and Romans 11:33
